items.question: What columns does the CSV have, and in what order and with what header names?
items.ticket: download their requisition list (with status and fill counts) as CSV
items.chose: Emits the header "Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created" with those six columns in that order.
items.instead: Use other header names or column order, such as snake_case field names, or omit Title or Created.

items.question: In what order are the rows emitted?
items.chose: Sorts a copy of the input by createdAt ascending, then by id ascending as a tie-break.
items.instead: Keep the caller's input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has an unknown status value?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id, and only the four statuses open, on_hold, filled and cancelled are accepted.
items.instead: Write the status through unchanged, or skip the row.

items.question: What happens when openings or filled is negative, fractional, NaN or infinite?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id. Both counts must be integers of at least 0.
items.instead: Write the number as-is, or clamp it to a valid value.

items.question: What happens when filled is greater than openings?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id.
items.instead: Export the row as-is, or cap filled at openings.

items.question: Is zero openings valid?
items.chose: Accepts openings of 0 (with filled 0) and writes the row normally.

items.question: What happens when createdAt is an invalid Date or not a Date?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id.
items.instead: Write an empty Created field, or skip the row.

items.question: Does one bad row fail the whole export or only that row?
items.chose: Validates every row first and throws on the first bad one, so no partial output is returned.
items.instead: Skip bad rows and export the rest, or collect all errors and report them together.

items.question: How is a missing or null title written?
items.chose: Writes an empty field for an undefined or null title.
items.instead: Write the literal text "null" or "undefined", or throw.

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks written?
items.chose: Wraps the field in double quotes and doubles any inner quotes, following RFC 4180.
items.instead: Quote every field, or leave fields unescaped.

items.question: Are spreadsheet formula characters (=, +, -, @) at the start of a field neutralised?
items.chose: Does nothing special. Titles starting with = or + are written as-is, apart from normal CSV quoting.
items.instead: Prefix such values with a single quote, or a tab, to prevent CSV formula injection.

items.question: What line endings, byte-order mark and trailing newline does the file use?
items.chose: Starts with a UTF-8 BOM, ends every line including the last with CRLF, and returns only the header and BOM for an empty list.
items.instead: Use LF endings, no BOM, and no trailing newline after the last row.
